After playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]], he was selected with the 32nd pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. ==Early life and education== Reed was born in [[Ewing Township, New Jersey]], on June 11, 1995. ===High school career=== A resident of [[Ewing Township, New Jersey]], Reed attended [[Princeton Day School]] from 2009 to 2013.Miller, Sean. [http://www.nj.com/times-sports/index.ssf/2017/06/former_pds_player_davon_reed_d.html "Former Princeton Day star Davon Reed taken 32nd in NBA Draft by Suns"], ''[[The Times (Trenton)|The Times]]'', June 23, 2017. Accessed June 27, 2017. "People knew Davon Reed was a special basketball player from the time he was a kid.... Ewing's Reed went to the Suns with the second pick of the second round, after Phoenix took Josh Jackson of Kansas with the fourth overall pick."{{Cite web |date=2017-06-22 |title=Phoenix Suns select former Princeton Day star Davon Reed in second round |url=https://www.trentonian.com/2017/06/22/phoenix-suns-select-former-princeton-day-star-davon-reed-in-second-round/ |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=Trentonian |language=en-US}} In his four-year career, Reed would score 2102 points at PDS, the highest in the school's history.{{Cite web |title=PDS Boys' Hoops Drops Nailbiter in Prep B Final But Reed's Heroics Lifted Panthers Into Spotlight {{!}} Town Topics |url=https://www.towntopics.com/wordpress/2013/02/27/pds-boys-hoops-drops-nailbiter-in-prep-b-final-but-reeds-heroics-lifted-panthers-into-spotlight/ |access-date=2022-09-29 |language=en-US}} ===College career=== [[File:Davon Reed (cropped).jpg|thumb|250px|Davon Reed handles the ball for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Hurricanes]].]] Reed attended the [[University of Miami]] from 2013 to 2017.{{Cite web |date=2017-06-02 |title=Davon Reed |url=https://miamihurricanes.com/roster/davon-reed/ |access-date=2022-09-29 |website=University of Miami Athletics |language=en-US}} He averaged 10.3 points and 3.6 rebounds per game throughout four seasons of playing time, with his best averages being 14.9 points and 4.8 rebounds in his last season for Miami. Reed developed a reputation as a good shooter who can defend four positions.{{cite news|last1=Kaufman|first1=Michelle|title=Hurricanes' Reed projected as a late second-rounder by some experts|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article157436154.html|access-date=23 June 2017|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=21 June 2017}} As a senior he was named to the [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] Third Team and All-Atlantic Coast Conference Defensive Team, as well as earned the Skip Prosser Award for Scholar Athletes.{{cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards-03-05-2017|title=ACC Announces All-Conference Team, Postseason Awards, All-ACC Teams|website=Theacc.com|author=Press Release|date=2017-03-05|access-date=2016-03-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170306210527/http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards-03-05-2017|archive-date=2017-03-06|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Phoenix Suns (2017–2018)=== Reed was selected as the 32nd pick of the [[2017 NBA Draft|2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/draft/phoenix-suns-draft-davon-reed-32nd-pick|title=Phoenix Suns Draft Davon Reed with the 32nd Pick - Phoenix Suns|website=Nba.com|access-date=19 October 2018}} He joined fellow rookies [[Josh Jackson (basketball)|Josh Jackson]] and [[Alec Peters]] in the [[2017 NBA Summer League]] alongside Suns' players [[Dragan Bender]], [[Marquese Chriss]], [[Tyler Ulis]], and [[Derrick Jones Jr.]]{{cite web|url=http://www.arizonasports.com/story/1165849/phoenix-suns-announce-roster-nba-summer-league-las-vegas/|title=Phoenix Suns announce roster for NBA Summer League in Las Vegas|date=3 July 2017|website=Arizonasports.com|access-date=19 October 2018}} Reed signed a four-year deal with the Suns on July 6, 2017.{{cite web|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2017/7/6/15931506/phoenix-suns-sign-davon-reed-nba-summer-league-las-vegas-a-guy-that-likes-defense-thats-pretty-cool|title=Suns sign Davon Reed to 4 year deal, fully guaranteed in 2017-18|website=Brightideaofthesun.com|date=6 July 2017|access-date=19 October 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-davon-reed|title=Phoenix Suns Sign Davon Reed - Phoenix Suns|website=Nba.com|access-date=19 October 2018}} In the 2017 Summer League, Reed recorded averages of 14.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists, and 1.2 steals per game in six games. On August 25, 2017, it was announced that Reed would have surgery on his left meniscus and miss the next four to six months.{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/08/25/phoenix-suns-davon-reed-miami-knee-injury/601544001/|title=Phoenix Suns rookie Reed out up to six months with knee injury|website=Azcentral.com|access-date=19 October 2018}} On December 28, Reed was assigned to the [[Motor City Cruise|Northern Arizona Suns]]. He played his first professional game with Northern Arizona on January 2, 2018, recording 11 points, 3 assists, and 2 rebounds in 20 minutes of play during a 113–108 win over the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]]. He played one more game on January 5 recording 10 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists in 22 minutes during a 125–104 win over the [[Reno Bighorns]] before being called up to Phoenix the next day. However, he did not play for Phoenix and was reassigned to Northern Arizona on January 8. He returned to Phoenix after the annual [[NBA G League]] Showcase on January 12. Reed made his NBA debut with Phoenix on January 14, recording a rebound in less than four minutes of play during a blowout loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He returned to Northern Arizona on January 21 and then back to Phoenix six days later. He recorded his first assist in a loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on January 29 before recording his first basket (via three-pointer) and a steal in a loss to the [[Utah Jazz]] on February 2. On March 10, after completing more assignments in Northern Arizona, Reed had his best game with Phoenix recording a season-high 16 points, making all four of his three-point shots, 6 rebounds, and 2 assists in a 122–115 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. On July 1, 2018, Reed was added to the Phoenix Suns' [[2018 NBA Summer League]] team alongside the majority of the team's young squad.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-announce-2018-summer-league-roster|title=Suns Announce 2018 Summer League Roster - Phoenix Suns|website=Nba.com|access-date=19 October 2018}} In the team's first Summer League game, Reed scored 18 points, including 4 of 5 three-pointers made, 3 rebounds, 2 steals, an assist, and a block in a 92–85 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. The next day, Reed recorded 12 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2 steals in a 71–63 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]]. At the end of the event, Reed averaged 13.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3 assists, and 0.8 steals per game{{cite web|url=https://stats.nba.com/summer-league/team/15/suns/|title=NBA Summer League|website=NBA Stats|access-date=19 October 2018|archive-date=21 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180721103332/https://stats.nba.com/summer-league/team/15/suns/|url-status=dead}} and Phoenix guaranteed his contract for a second year.{{cite web|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2018/7/20/17595006/phoenix-suns-guarantee-guard-davon-reed-for-2018-19-season|title=Phoenix Suns guarantee guard Davon Reed for 2018-19 season|website=Brightsideofthesun.com|date=20 July 2018|access-date=19 October 2018}} However, on October 16, 2018, Reed was waived by the [[Phoenix Suns]] and replaced on the roster by veteran [[Jamal Crawford]].{{cite web |title=Phoenix Suns Sign Jamal Crawford |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-jamal-crawford |date=October 17, 2018 |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 17, 2018}} ===Indiana Pacers (2018–2019)=== On October 19, three days after being waived by the Suns, Reed signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Indiana Pacers]] and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-davon-reed|title=Pacers Sign Davon Reed|website=[[NBA.com]] }} He filled the roster spot held by [[C. J. Wilcox]] after he suffered a season-ending injury. ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2019–2020)=== On September 4, 2019, Reed signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=HEAT Signs Davon Reed|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-davon-reed-190904|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 4, 2019|date=September 4, 2019}} Following training camp, Reed was added to the roster of the Heat's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite news |title= Skyforce Announces 2019–20 Training Camp Roster |url= https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-2019-20-training-camp-roster/ |access-date= November 2, 2019 |work= [[NBA.com]] |date= October 27, 2019 |archive-date= November 2, 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191102180042/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-2019-20-training-camp-roster/ |url-status= dead }} On February 5, 2020, Reed posted 29 points, 11 rebounds, eight assists and three steals for Sioux Falls in a 123–117 loss to the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite news |title=Davon Reed: Huge outing in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/davon-reed-huge-outing-in-g-league/ |access-date=February 6, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 6, 2020}} Reed averaged 12.7 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game and became the only player in the G League to have at least 500 points, 250 rebounds and 150 assists.{{cite news |last1=Dykstra |first1=Matt |title=Davon Reed Joins 500-250-150 Club Prior to G League Hiatus |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/davon-reed-joins-500-250-150-club-prior-to-g-league-hiatus/ |access-date=June 13, 2020 |work=NBA.com |date=April 13, 2020 |archive-date=October 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027182749/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/davon-reed-joins-500-250-150-club-prior-to-g-league-hiatus/ |url-status=dead }} ===Taoyuan Pilots (2020–2021)=== In November 2020, Reed joined the [[Taoyuan Pilots]] of the [[P. League+]].{{cite news |title=領航猿雙洋將曝光！2017選秀大年3D射手入列 |url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/3357717 |access-date=28 September 2021 |work=Liberty Times |date=2020-11-20}} In April 2021,
